edits.text: - If the left-side stretch is read alone, is it a coherent, self-contained proposition? Most severe when the cut severs a head (a verb or a noun) from an immediately following essential complement or modifier — e.g. an obligatory object, required prepositional phrase, infinitival or a that/which/who clause — or when attachment is left unresolved; mildest when the cut leaves the left span a grammatically complete unit (a full independent clause or an entire noun phrase), as when splitting between coordinate list items or after a complete clause.
edits._was: - If the left-side stretch is read alone, is it a coherent, self-contained proposition? The worst are fragments that lack a diagnosable main predicate or identity of agent when isolated; the mildest are independent clauses, appositives, or clearly parenthetical material that preserve truth when isolated.

edits.text: When two candidate cuts fall inside the same attachment chain, prefer the cut that leaves the left span a grammatically complete unit (an independent clause or an entire NP) over the cut that leaves a fragment.
edits._was: - When one cut falls between a verb and its obligatory object/complement and another falls earlier within pre-verbal adjunct material, prefer the later cut after the complement.

edits.text: - Is this marker immediately before an essential complement or modifier that completes the preceding noun or verb? Most severe when it severs a head (verb or noun) from a required complement — an obligatory object, an essential prepositional phrase, an infinitival or other verbal complement, or a that/which/who relative clause; mildest when the following material is parenthetical, coordinate, or when the left span is already a grammatically complete clause or full noun phrase.
edits._was: - Will translating the left and right sides separately then joining them preserve the whole sentence meaning? Severe failures occur when the following words determine attachment, scope, or core argument roles; mild cases are when both sides are semantically independent lists or coordinate items.

edits.text: When two candidate cuts fall inside the same attachment chain, prefer the cut that leaves the left span a grammatically complete unit (an independent clause or an entire NP) over the cut that leaves a fragment.

- Is this marker placed between a head (a verb or a noun) and an immediately following essential complement or modifier that completes it? Keep the head together with the complement that completes it: most severe when the following span is an obligatory complement (direct object, required prepositional complement, infinitival or that-clause, or a restrictive relative) whose attachment determines core argument or scope; mildest when the following material is parenthetical, optional/nonrestrictive, a coordinate/list item, or when the left span already forms a grammatically complete clause or full NP.

edits._was: - When one marker detaches a relative clause from its head noun and another splits inside that relative clause, prefer the cut inside the relative clause.
